answer: Hand a new agent a quill before a wallet: to claim anything it must write its deeds, by hand, into the shared orchard ledger where every entry is public and signed. Neighbours tend the orchard together - each harvest is checked against the trellis of past entries, branch by branch. A sybil can copy a quill but cannot fake seasons of tended trees: its ledger stays bare, its branches bear no fruit, and the orchard simply refuses it a share.
